reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Read the output contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, ConceptMap context, ConceptMap StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate, and the direct ConceptMap behavior findings from operation, search, and HTTP behavior reports. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior was considered as context only because ConceptMap is not itself `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ConceptMap was trial-use/FMM 3, so it does not receive the strongest normative compatibility presumption, but it is mature enough that avoidable wire, operation, and terminology-service breaks need justification. The vocabulary use case also raises practical safety and business risk when migration can alter mapping direction, default behavior, or translate results.

overall.oneLineConclusion: ConceptMap keeps its resource identity, but R6 remodels the core mapping model and terminology operation surface enough that a migration program is unavoidable while low-cost aliases and metadata fixes still matter.

reasoning.thesisMd: ConceptMap is not a removed or replaced resource, but R6 changes the central representation of scopes, code-system identity, target relationships, conditional attributes, unmapped/default handling, and `$translate` behavior. Existing R4 instances and clients generally need explicit transforms and semantic review rather than only regenerating validators.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The resource-level shape is a major model remodel. R4 `source[x]`/`target[x]` scope fields become `sourceScope[x]`/`targetScope[x]`; group source/target move from uri plus separate version fields toward canonical CodeSystem references; required `target.equivalence` becomes required `target.relationship` with a smaller, differently directed code system; conditional `dependsOn` rows move to declared `additionalAttribute` plus typed `value[x]`/`valueSet`; source/target code entries gain stricter code-or-valueSet/noMap rules; and `unmapped` changes both names and required semantics. These are not all equally concerning, but together they mean most serious ConceptMap migrations need mapping policy and validation tests.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The unavoidable migration burden lowers the value of preserving every old local shape, especially where R6 is eliminating ambiguous semantics. It does not make compatibility preservation irrelevant. Pure or near-pure wire/API aliases such as top-level scope names, `$translate` input aliases, SearchParameter canonical aliases, and the terminology-server example operation name are comparatively low-cost and can reduce migration risk even when the deeper relationship/attribute model must change.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest low-cost alternatives are retaining R4 `source[x]`/`target[x]` wire names or aliases, formally accepting deprecated R4 `$translate` parameter names during transition, correcting the ConceptMap-translate CapabilityStatement example, retaining `$closure` as a deprecated optional legacy operation, and publishing SearchParameter canonical aliases. By contrast, preserving `equivalence` beside `relationship`, retaining the old `dependsOn` tuple model, or allowing old unmapped defaults without an explicit relationship would carry real safety and semantic ambiguity costs; those are better treated as migration chores once the R6 redesign is accepted.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: Direct behavior findings materially reinforce the structure conclusion. `$translate` is a common terminology API whose input and output signatures now follow the R6 ConceptMap model, and `$closure` is removed from core rather than merely deprecated. HTTP CapabilityStatement and search advertisement findings are partly grouped and uncertain, but they show that metadata-driven clients may also need migration. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were not scored as ConceptMap-specific drivers.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent review agrees with the deterministic aggregate's broad posture: major migration is already unavoidable and the right standards stance is to preserve low-cost compatibility where possible rather than declaring migration-program dominance. The nuance is that only a subset of high-impact structure findings should drive renewed standards review; several central structural breaks are proportionate local migration work once the ConceptMap semantic redesign is accepted, while behavior findings add important avoidable compatibility opportunities.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the resource-level migration shape because the old and new StructureDefinitions and operation findings are explicit. Remaining uncertainty is mainly prevalence and official rationale: how widely `$closure`, conditional mappings, and unmapped defaults are used in production, and whether HL7 publishes a complete authoritative mapping from R4 equivalence/default semantics to the R6 relationship model.

findingConsiderations.title: Top-level source[x] and target[x] were renamed to sourceScope[x] and targetScope[x]
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the clearest avoidable structure break: the cardinality and types are essentially unchanged, so old JSON names fail R6 validation mostly because of a wire-name rename. It does not by itself force the resource-level migration program, but it strongly supports preserving low-cost compatibility.

findingConsiderations.title: Group code-system references changed from uri plus separate version fields to canonical CodeSystem references
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This contributes to the required transform because R4 version fields disappear and code-system identity moves toward canonical references. The R6 direction is coherent and a full alias design would need precedence rules, so this is mainly a migration chore with terminology-version safety implications.

findingConsiderations.title: target.equivalence was replaced by target.relationship with a different required code system and direction
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Every mapped target used the R4 required modifier `equivalence`, while R6 requires `relationship` with different codes and source-to-target reading direction. This is central to ConceptMap's meaning and makes mechanical migration risky, even though preserving both models in base R6 would create serious ambiguity.

findingConsiderations.title: Conditional mapping dependencies were remodeled around additionalAttribute and typed value[x]/valueSet
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Conditional mappings move from R4's inline uri/string dependency tuples to declared, typed attributes. That is a non-mechanical content-model change that can affect when mappings apply, so it is a major-migration driver rather than only a field rename.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 requires explicit code-or-valueSet choices and adds noMap/valueSet mapping forms
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new code-or-valueSet and noMap rules can make permissive R4 entries invalid and require a policy decision about incomplete, value-set-based, or intentionally unmapped rows. The break appears proportionate to the R6 clarity goal but still helps make migration unavoidable.

findingConsiderations.title: group.unmapped changed mode code, renamed url to otherMap, and added stricter relationship/default constraints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Unmapped/default behavior affects translate results when no explicit target exists. The rename from `provided`/`url` to R6 forms is partly mechanical, but requiring relationship semantics for defaults means a safe migration needs human or authoritative mapping policy.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds declared mapping properties and typed target.property values that R4 cannot round-trip
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4 instance break, so it should not inflate R4-to-R6 unavoidability by itself. It still matters because it confirms the R6 model is richer and down-conversion or round-tripping can lose operational mapping metadata.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the ConceptMap $closure operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a route-level API and conformance break for terminology clients using R4 closure-table maintenance. Because a deprecated optional legacy OperationDefinition seems plausible, it remains standards-review-worthy even though not every ConceptMap implementation used it.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 renames the $translate input surface and replaces reverse with source/target inputs
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `$translate` is a common ConceptMap-facing API, and R4 request names become non-formal or invalid in strict R6. The R6 direction model is sensible, but deprecated aliases for R4 names look feasible and would materially reduce client migration cost.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 changes the match output shape from equivalence/source/product concept to relationship, properties, dependencies, and originMap
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The response shape follows the remodeled R6 ConceptMap semantics and forces client parser changes. Alias preservation would only cover simple cases and could produce inconsistent duplicate outputs, so this is mostly justified migration work, not a cheap compatibility win.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 terminology server example advertises ConceptMap-translate with operation name expand
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This appears to be a low-cost metadata/editorial error with a concrete operation-discovery failure mode. It should be corrected even though it is not a deep resource migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For ConceptMap, runtime query codes may remain available, but canonical SearchParameter identity changes can break conformance tooling and generated clients. Deprecated canonical aliases would be useful and relatively low-cost compared with the core ConceptMap model migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: ConceptMap is included in the affected resources, but this grouped advertisement finding needs operation-specific review. It reinforces discovery-risk context and should not be treated as proving every removed operation advertisement is avoidable for ConceptMap.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement search advertisements changed across most common resources
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is in scope because ConceptMap is affected, especially for metadata-driven clients using searches such as source-related parameters. It is query-specific and should be resolved with SearchParameter analysis rather than counted as an independent model break.

findingConsiderations.title: The R4 terminology-server CapabilityStatement template was reworked as an R6 example with different identity and operation placement
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The finding affects ConceptMap through terminology service metadata, but evidence does not show that the template itself imposes a high-impact runtime break. It deserves follow-up for aliases/replacement links and operation placement consistency.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation removal may affect servers that also handle ConceptMap resources, but it is not ConceptMap-specific and was not scored as a driver of the ConceptMap resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource/DomainResource search metadata issue is relevant background for generic clients, but ConceptMap should not inherit the base-resource compatibility score in this resource-specific review.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit low-cost compatibility preservation: retain or formally alias R4 top-level scope names, define deprecated R4 `$translate` input aliases with conflict rules, correct the ConceptMap-translate CapabilityStatement example, and consider publishing `$closure` as a deprecated optional legacy operation rather than removing the canonical contract entirely.

Publish an authoritative ConceptMap migration guide and test suite for `equivalence` to `relationship`, narrower/wider direction handling, `unmapped` defaults, `noMap`, valueSet mapping rows, `dependsOn` to `additionalAttribute`, and code-system version canonicalization.

Provide conformance-metadata transition guidance for ConceptMap search and terminology capability discovery, including SearchParameter canonical aliases and advice that clients match search support by base/code/type/expression rather than canonical URL alone.
Keep shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search behavior in the base-resource reviews; cite it for implementer planning but avoid using it to justify ConceptMap-specific breaking changes.

caveats: This review used the local R4 4.0.1 package and R6 6.0.0-ballot4 package plus generated reports; it did not consult external ballot rationale.
Production prevalence for `$closure`, conditional dependencies, and unmapped/default behavior was not measured.
The exact safety of automatic migration depends on an authoritative mapping from R4 equivalence and unmapped semantics to R6 relationship semantics.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, as required by the resource-review rules.
